thread:
IncidentBot: P1 alert — traffic spike: ~30% of embedding requests returning 500s. Possible model fallback loop detected. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:
Alex R.: seeing a bunch of 500s from embedding-service, linking to routing logs now.
Mira Chen: confirming — large batch of requests from eu-west-1 routed to a chat/instruct variant. That variant rejects embedding payloads (schema mismatch) and bubbles up 500s.
Sam P.: who pushed the alias/anchor change? any recent rollout?
Kat L.: I did a quick grep — alias embeddings-prod currently anchored to model: redwood-model-v2-chat-2026@variant-instruct. That looks wrong.
Nate V.: paging history shows a rollout 12m ago from deploy-bot: alias-update embeddings-prod -> v2-chat.
Alex R.: Customer impact: three tenants seeing degraded ingest: SearchPulse, QueryCo, internal-kv-indexer. Alerting CS.
Mira Chen: can we immediate-override routing for embeddings to fallback to the previous embeddings-optimized variant? Temporary route + block anchoring.
Sam P.: I can apply an emergency routing override. Will push a policy that forces content-type=embedding -> model: redwood-embed-v1 (compatible).
Kat L.: please also remove the pinned alias so no automatic re-anchoring.
Alex R.: paste the command you'll run so oncall can audit.
Sam P.: running: ```
# emergency routing override (k8s config apply)
kubectl -n routing apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: routing.redwood/v1
kind: RoutingOverride
metadata:
  name: emergency-emb-override-1765559876
spec:
  match:
    content_type: "embedding"
  action:
    route_to: "redwood-embed-v1"
    ttl_seconds: 900
EOF
```
Nate V.: also blocking alias change: ```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/anchors/block \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"alias":"embeddings-prod","reason":"emergency-block-1765559876"}'
```
deploy-bot: rollout: alias-update embeddings-prod -> redwood-embed-v1 (override) by Sam P. — started at 1765559932
Alex R.: routing logs show immediate drop in 500s after 1765559945. Metrics: embedding error rate down from 28% -> 2% within 90s.
Mira Chen: CS pinged impacted tenants, they see improvement, leaving monitoring window.
Kat L.: root cause hypothesis: a deploy script mistakenly used a shared alias variable and pointed embeddings-prod at a chat variant during a rapid canary for a chat-only model. No safety check for content-type compatibility in the alias change.
Sam P.: I found the change: prior pipeline job "alias-rollout-chat-canary" had a collision (env var ALIAS=embeddings-prod). Fixing pipeline to require explicit target list.
Nate V.: opened ticket INFRA-2247 to add a preflight compatibility check for alias updates (verify model capabilities include "embeddings" when alias is embeddings-*).
Alex R.: we should also add an automated gating rule: alias updates to embedding aliases must fail if target model capability != embeddings.
Mira Chen: for immediate mitigation we added the TTL 900s override and blocked the alias. Will plan a controlled re-anchoring after compatibility tests.
Sam P.: do we need to rollback any deploys? The chat canary itself is fine — only the alias collision was bad. No other services impacted.
Kat L.: double-checking: no data exfil, no customer prompts exposed. This was a routing mis-anchor only.
Alex R.: timeline/notes for postmortem: 1) 1765559876 alert fired; 2) 1765559932 override applied; 3) 1765559945 error-rate drop observed; 4) 1765560000 monitoring window green but still under watch.
Nate V.: CS update prepared: "We experienced degraded embeddings for a subset of tenants due to an internal routing config error; fixes applied and services restored. We will follow up with a technical postmortem and compensatory credits if needed."
Mira Chen: thanks everyone — handoff to postmortem owners: Kat + Nate. Oncall relieved at 1765560000.
Alex R.: one more action: add a synthetic embedding check to canary pipelines to catch this earlier. Filed as INFRA-2248.
Sam P.: adding blocker to the alias rollout job to require capability matching.
deploy-bot: action complete: emergency override removed TTL expiry scheduled.
IncidentBot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. P1 -> degraded.
Kat L.: I'll own the timeline and postmortem, will collect logs and comms.
Nate V.: will draft the customer note and coordinate with CS.
Alex R.: thanks team. :thumbsup:
